title: Count Equal and Divisible Pairs in an Array
summary: For an array of integers nums of length n and an integer k, count the pairs (i, j) where 0 <= i < j < n, such that the elements at these indices are equal and the product of their indices is divisible by k.
statement: For an array of integers nums of length n and an integer k, count the pairs (i, j) where 0 <= i < j < n, such that the elements at these indices are equal and the product of their indices is divisible by k.
constraints: Count index pairs with 0 <= i < j < len(nums).
The values nums[i] and nums[j] must be equal.
The index product i*j, not the value product, must be divisible by k.
hints: The constraints allow checking every index pair directly.
Use nested indices and test both required predicates.
For each right index, scan all earlier left indices and increment when values match and left*right is divisible by k.
Every valid ordered index pair i<j appears exactly once in the nested loops.
editorial: Every valid ordered index pair i<j appears exactly once in the nested loops.

tests.explanation: Four equal-value pairs also have an index product divisible by two.
Every index product is divisible by one, but no values match, so return zero.
